findings_qualitative.value: High Doppler velocity wings up to ~20 km s^-1 are present in both blue-shifted and red-shifted hemispheres near the line of sight crossing R Doradus, particularly visible in CO, SiO, and SO, and accelerated at ~0.68 ± 0.10 km s^-1 au^-1.

evidence.quote: They are present in both blue-shifted and red-shifted hemispheres but are not exactly back-to-back. They are accelerated at a typical rate of 0.7 km s−1 au−1 up to some 20 km s−1.

findings_qualitative.value: The high-velocity wings are not artefacts of continuum subtraction, and they show remarkable symmetry in intensity between the blue-shifted and red-shifted wings in continuum-unsubtracted SiO spectra.

evidence.loc: III.2. Eliminating a possible effect related to continuum subtraction
evidence.quote: This result gives confidence in the reality of the high Doppler velocity components, seen to rise above continuum emission below |Vz| ∼ 20 km s−1. It displays a remarkable symmetry between blue-shifted and red-shifted wings, at variance with an earlier interpretation of the “blue blob” as causing one-sided ejection of material [28].

findings_qualitative.value: No fully convincing physical interpretation (gas streams, rotation, or stellar pulsations) can currently explain the high-velocity wings without significant difficulties; turbulence on the Earth side of the stellar atmosphere is a possible unexplored alternative.

evidence.quote: We conclude that, in the state of current knowledge, no fully convincing picture of the physics governing the production of such high velocities, typically twice as large as the terminal velocity, can be reliably drawn.

A possibility that has not been seriously explored would be that the large Doppler velocities, rather than revealing large radial wind velocities, would instead reveal large line widths caused by turbulence, which would then be dominantly detected on the Earth side of the star atmosphere and would provide a simple explanation for the nearly perfect blue-red symmetry displayed in Figure 6.

claims.hypothesis: The high Doppler velocity wings in R Doradus can be described as a pair of accelerating gas streams emitted near the line of sight, similar to those in EP Aqr, rather than a one-sided blob.
claims.experiment: Constructed integrated P-V maps, integrated intensity maps for |Vz| > 7.5 km s^-1, channel maps, and transverse spatial profiles for five molecular lines (CO, SiO, SO, SO2, HCN).
claims.result: High-velocity features reach |Vz| ~ 20 km s^-1 in both blue- and red-shifted hemispheres with a mean projected acceleration of 0.68 ± 0.10 km s^-1 au^-1 and deconvolved transverse widths of 70 mas in x and 90 mas in y, though the red-shifted component stays within ~10 au projected while the blue-shifted component extends to ~30 au, and the line of sight plays no special symmetry role in R Dor.
claims.finding: The high-velocity features are continuous with the slow wind and present on both sides (not one-sided), consistent morphologically with nearly back-to-back streams, but their alignment near the line of sight (at a large angle to proposed stellar/disc rotation axes) and red-blue spatial asymmetry cast doubt on a simple gas stream interpretation.

evidence.quote: However, in contrast to EP Aqr, the line of sight plays no particular role in the R Dor morpho-kinematics, shedding doubt on the validity of a gas stream interpretation.

evidence.loc: III.1. Interpretation in terms of gas streams
evidence.quote: The interpretation of the high Doppler velocity components as streams rather than blobs is justified from their continuity with the slow wind: they only appear as blobs when considering a slice confined to an interval of Doppler velocity.
Evidence has been obtained for a possible description of the nascent wind of AGB star R Dor in terms of a pair of high velocity gas streams emitted nearly back-to-back near the line of sight.

claims.hypothesis: The high Doppler velocity wings emitted near the line of sight are artefacts caused by improper continuum subtraction in the uv plane.
claims.experiment: Re-analysed raw archival SiO(8-7) visibility data from two datasets with different uv coverage without subtracting the continuum, and examined the resulting Doppler velocity spectra for |Vz| > 8 km s^-1 in R < 1.5 arcsec and R < 0.3 arcsec apertures.
claims.result: Uniform continuum emission is seen at 0.60 ± 0.03 Jy for |Vz| > 20 km s^-1, and symmetric blue- and red-shifted high-velocity wings clearly rise above the continuum level below |Vz| ~ 20 km s^-1 within R < 0.3 arcsec.
claims.finding: Improper continuum subtraction is ruled out as the cause of the high Doppler velocity wings.

evidence.quote: We exclude an effect of improper continuum subtraction.

evidence.loc: III.2. Eliminating a possible effect related to continuum subtraction
evidence.quote: This result gives confidence in the reality of the high Doppler velocity components, seen to rise above continuum emission below |Vz| ∼ 20 km s−1.
This may suggest that they be artefacts of improper data reduction and/or continuum subtraction but an analysis of continuum-unsubstracted data confirms the validity of the gas stream interpretation.

claims.hypothesis: The high Doppler velocity wings in R Doradus can be explained by gas rotation (Keplerian disc or solid body shell rotation) or a pulsating spherical shell.
claims.experiment: Compared the observed 20 km s^-1 velocity reach, spatial confinement (< 18-30 au), and red-blue spatial asymmetry against the Keplerian rotation model of Homan et al. (2018b), the solid-body rotation model of Vlemmings et al. (2018), and expanding spherical shell geometry.
claims.result: Keplerian rotation requires 20 km s^-1 to occur at ~2.2 au (near the stellar surface, undetected in v=1 SiO), solid-body rotation places 20 km s^-1 at ~38 au (nearly twice the observed limit), a pulsating shell requires a radius <= 15-20 au, and both rotation and pulsation predict spatial red-blue symmetry contrary to observations.
claims.finding: Interpretations in terms of rotation or stellar pulsations face major difficulties and cannot be retained with confidence; no fully convincing physical picture currently exists.

evidence.loc: III.3. Interpretations in terms of pulsations or rotations
evidence.quote: Both interpretations, rotation and pulsation, predict red-blue symmetry in contrast with what is observed.
Moreover, interpretations in terms of rotation or pulsations have been shown to meet important difficulties that prevent retaining such interpretations with reasonable confidence.
However, today, no fully convincing interpretation of the physics governing their existence can be reliably proposed.

why_this_data.value: Archival ALMA observations of five molecular lines (CO, SiO, SO, SO2, HCN) probe distances between ~10 and ~100 au in the nascent wind of R Doradus with high angular resolution (~150 mas), where high-velocity wings had been noted by Decin et al. (2018) and where SO data had not yet been analysed for high velocities.

evidence.quote: We probe distances from the star between ∼10 and ∼100 au using ALMA observations of the emission of five different molecular lines.
These data have not been used by other authors and the study of Nhung et al. (2019b) [21] does not address the issue of large Doppler velocity components.
They have been used by Decin et al. (2018) [5] who show channel maps but do not perform a detailed analysis of the large Doppler velocity components.

why_this_method.value: Integrating P-V maps over the full perpendicular spatial axis reveals global phase-space confinement, defining |Vz| > 7.5 km s^-1 separates the high-velocity wings from the dominant slow wind, and re-imaging SiO without continuum subtraction directly tests whether uv continuum subtraction creates line-of-sight velocity wing artefacts.

evidence.loc: III.1. Interpretation in terms of gas streams
evidence.quote: We define large Doppler velocity components as having |Vz| > 7.5 km s−1 in order to separate them from the slower wind.

evidence.loc: III.2. Eliminating a possible effect related to continuum subtraction
evidence.quote: In order to check on this, we repeated the analysis of the SiO observations without performing any continuum subtraction, namely Fourier-transforming directly the measured visibilities.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Improper continuum subtraction in the uv plane producing line-of-sight artefacts (rejected by re-reducing SiO data without continuum subtraction).

evidence.loc: III.2. Eliminating a possible effect related to continuum subtraction
evidence.quote: In order to check on this, we repeated the analysis of the SiO observations without performing any continuum subtraction, namely Fourier-transforming directly the measured visibilities.
This may suggest that they be artefacts of improper data reduction and/or continuum subtraction but an analysis of continuum-unsubstracted data confirms the validity of the gas stream interpretation.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: One-sided ejection of material for the 'blue blob' (rejected because continuum-unsubtracted SiO spectra show symmetric blue-shifted and red-shifted wings).

evidence.loc: III.2. Eliminating a possible effect related to continuum subtraction
evidence.quote: It displays a remarkable symmetry between blue-shifted and red-shifted wings, at variance with an earlier interpretation of the “blue blob” as causing one-sided ejection of material [28].

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Keplerian rotation or solid body shell rotation (rejected due to mismatch in radial distance where 20 km s^-1 is reached and lack of observed spatial red-blue symmetry).

evidence.loc: III.3. Interpretations in terms of pulsations or rotations
evidence.quote: Keplerian rotation would imply that the maximal observed velocity of 20 km s−1 would be reached at only ∼2.2 au from the star centre, very close to the stellar surface.

evidence.loc: III.3. Interpretations in terms of pulsations or rotations
evidence.quote: Vlemmings et al. (2018) [28] quote a solid body rotation of 1.0±0.1 km s−1 at the stellar surface (∼1.9 au) meaning that a rotation velocity of 20 km s−1 would be reached at a distance of ∼38 au from the star, nearly twice as far as the canonical limit that has been set.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Pulsating spherical shell (rejected on the basis of Nowotny et al. 2010 model and observed spatial red-blue asymmetry).

evidence.loc: III.3. Interpretations in terms of pulsations or rotations
evidence.quote: An interpretation in terms of a pulsating spherical shell is equally challenging. It has been explicitly excluded by Decin et al. (2018) [5] on the basis of a model [22].

evidence.loc: III.3. Interpretations in terms of pulsations or rotations
evidence.quote: Both interpretations, rotation and pulsation, predict red-blue symmetry in contrast with what is observed.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Large line widths caused by turbulence on the Earth side of the stellar atmosphere (proposed as an unexplored alternative).

evidence.quote: A possibility that has not been seriously explored would be that the large Doppler velocities, rather than revealing large radial wind velocities, would instead reveal large line widths caused by turbulence, which would then be dominantly detected on the Earth side of the star atmosphere and would provide a simple explanation for the nearly perfect blue-red symmetry displayed in Figure 6.

limitations_admitted.value: Different datasets in project 2013.1.00166.S have significantly different uv coverage and maximum recoverable scales, causing important differences in flux density in the slow wind region.

evidence.quote: These observations, reduced using the results of the standard ALMA pipeline, include datasets associated with significantly different uv coverage, implying different maximal recoverable scales. While this implies important differences in the flux-density measured in the region of the slow wind, we have checked that very similar results are instead obtained in the region of large Doppler velocities explored here at small projected distance from the star.

limitations_admitted.value: Inability to determine the 3D longitudinal extension of the streams along the line of sight without assuming an arbitrary length scale.

evidence.loc: III.1. Interpretation in terms of gas streams
evidence.quote: Of course, these numbers scale with the arbitrary length of 60 au used in the example and are simply meant to illustrate a possible stream geometry.

limitations_admitted.value: Insufficient sensitivity may explain the lack of detection of HCN at large Doppler velocities.

evidence.loc: III.1. Interpretation in terms of gas streams
evidence.quote: the absence of detection at large Doppler velocities may simply be the result of insufficient sensitivity.

limitations_admitted.value: Complexity of the slow wind morpho-kinematics prevents establishing a reliable relation with the spectral depletions observed between -1 and 3 km s^-1 or the lower-|Vz| blue-shifted enhancement.

evidence.loc: III.1. Interpretation in terms of gas streams
evidence.quote: While the global picture is dominated by the former, which extends down to −20 km s−1 with intensity comparable to the red-shifted component, the presence of this enhancement cannot be ignored and needs to be studied in relation with the complex morpho-kinematics of the slow wind [21]. However, this is beyond the scope of the present work that focuses on the dominant large Doppler velocity components.

evidence.loc: III.1. Interpretation in terms of gas streams
evidence.quote: In the present case, the complexity of the observed morpho-kinematics [21] prevents from asserting reliably the existence of such a relation.

referee_caveats_inferred: The spatial alignment of the high-velocity wings along the line of sight in both EP Aqr and R Doradus (despite very different inferred disc/stellar rotation axes) strongly suggests an observational or radiative transfer effect along the line of sight (such as atmospheric turbulence or optical depth effects infront of the stellar continuum) rather than collimated physical jets happening to point at Earth in both stars.
No radiative transfer modelling is performed to test optical depth, excitation, or absorption effects against the stellar continuum.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~50-200 GB for raw visibility datasets of 2013.1.00166.S and 2017.1.00824.S; <5 GB for pipeline-reduced spectral cubes.
reproducibility.score_reason: The paper uses public ALMA archival data (mostly standard pipeline products) and performs straightforward geometric projections, velocity cuts, and 1D Gaussian fits with clearly stated coordinate rotations and velocity thresholds. However, software versions, exact spatial integration windows for the summed P-V maps, and specific execution block selections for project 2013.1.00166.S are not explicitly stated.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: All ALMA data are public in the archive (projects 2013.1.00166.S and 2017.1.00824.S), standard pipeline cubes can be used directly for the main analysis, and the key quantitative results (line peak intensities, slow-wind terminal velocities, high-velocity wing reach, projected acceleration, deconvolved stream widths, and continuum flux) are straightforward to re-measure.
